**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard against null route paths when prefixing mount points**

When a handler is registered on a pathless route (e.g., `router.route().handler(...)`), `currentRoute().getPath()` can be null, but this new branch concatenates `mountPoint + route` (or calls `route.substring(1)`), producing an invalid `http.route` like `"/apinull"` (or throwing if the mount point ends with `/`). In sub-routers this is common for middleware, and because `HttpServerRouteSource.NESTED_CONTROLLER` keeps the “best” (longest) route at the same priority, the bogus value can block later concrete route updates, leaving incorrect route attributes on spans/metrics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
